title: One Playbook, Three Capitals
thesis: Across Ankara, New Delhi, and Budapest the same sequence runs — contest the count, starve the critics, narrow the exits — a playbook that needs no author to coordinate it.
body:
The leaders do not coordinate, share an ideology, or in some cases even speak. Yet across three capitals this spring the same sequence runs: contest the count, starve the critics, narrow the exits [sy_410fc0a565c9, sy_197ff0249bcf, sy_ed4687a441a0].

<instances as="portraits">
<item>In Ankara, opposition mayors are detained weeks before a vote, decapitating the local machine that would run the campaign [sy_410fc0a565c9].</item>
<item>In New Delhi, foreign-funding rules are tightened until the NGOs that monitor elections cannot make payroll [sy_197ff0249bcf].</item>
<item>In Budapest, a financing move quietly defunds the last independent newsroom [sy_ed4687a441a0].</item>
</instances>

<card kind="actor">Recep Tayyip Erdoğan</card>
<card kind="actor">Viktor Orbán</card>

<quote display="card">[qt_779c708ac084]</quote>

It is a playbook precisely because it needs no author. Each move is locally legal, individually deniable, and only legible as a pattern when the three are laid side by side [sy_410fc0a565c9, sy_ed4687a441a0].

entities.name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
entities.role: President whose government detained opposition mayors before a vote.
entities.summary: **Recep Tayyip Erdoğan** has paired electoral contests with pre-emptive detentions of local opposition figures, a tactic critics call lawfare.

entities.name: Viktor Orbán
entities.role: Prime minister advancing measures that defund independent media.
entities.summary: **Viktor Orbán** is widely treated as the template for the playbook, having normalized the financial squeeze of independent newsrooms.

entities.name: Narendra Modi
entities.role: Prime minister whose government tightened NGO foreign-funding rules.
entities.summary: **Narendra Modi**'s administration has tightened the foreign-funding regime that election-monitoring NGOs depend on, framing it as a sovereignty measure.

entities.name: Nils Muiznieks
entities.role: Rights monitor who named the cross-border pattern.
entities.summary: **Nils Muiznieks** tracks the convergence of these tactics across unrelated governments and argues the resemblance is structural, not coordinated.
